source: Curated pairs/triples of actual captured sections from existing 141-module library

patterns.title: The product is the hero
patterns.question: How can a complex physical part become the strongest visual element?
patterns.principle: Let real objects, proportions, texture and technical details carry the identity.
patterns.compare: Compare the visual scale of a product against headline size, background and supporting copy.
patterns.when: For engineered components, machines, and industrial design portfolios.

patterns.title: Cinematic industrial photography
patterns.question: How do industrial sites create a memorable first impression without losing credibility?
patterns.principle: Use real machines and lighting with a simple message; avoid decorative mockups.
patterns.compare: Compare contrast, product visibility and CTA hierarchy.
patterns.when: For robotics, heavy equipment and advanced manufacturing.

patterns.title: Materials become the brand
patterns.question: How can texture and finish become a differentiated B2B visual system?
patterns.principle: Use the physical material's behavior, finish and context instead of abstract graphics.
patterns.compare: Compare crop choices, palettes and product texture.
patterns.when: For architectural materials, chemicals, textiles, and surfaces.

patterns.title: Real interface, not decoration
patterns.question: How do software and technical platforms show their value without vague imagery?
patterns.principle: Lead with an actual UI, scan or data experience, then explain what buyers can do with it.
patterns.compare: Compare interface legibility, technical depth and visual storytelling.
patterns.when: For engineering software, inspection platforms and technical SaaS.

patterns.title: Specification-first navigation
patterns.question: How can engineering buyers locate exact parts across thousands of options?
patterns.principle: Make categories and specifications primary and minimize promotional interference.
patterns.compare: Compare information density, category hierarchy and product findability.
patterns.when: For industrial components, tooling and technical distribution.

patterns.title: A complex equipment family
patterns.question: How do you structure a catalogue of hardware variants?
patterns.principle: Reveal product families before drilling down to model specifications.
patterns.compare: Compare family labels, product-image consistency and detail paths.
patterns.when: For machinery, robotics and equipment.

patterns.title: Manufacturing capabilities as a menu
patterns.question: How do buyers understand a multi-process factory without reading a long brochure?
patterns.principle: Group capabilities by manufacturing job or process, with a distinct route to each service.
patterns.compare: Compare use of real part imagery, process cards and action labels.
patterns.when: For contract manufacturers and on-demand production.

patterns.title: Discover by real applications
patterns.question: How should a technical site answer the customer's use case first?
patterns.principle: Give industry and application routes equal prominence with product technology.
patterns.compare: Compare application photography, audience framing and next actions.
patterns.when: For equipment with broad cross-industry use.

patterns.title: Immediate quotation paths
patterns.question: When should a B2B website lead with instant pricing or a direct RFQ?
patterns.principle: Make the first conversion step unmistakable, while providing supporting capability proof.
patterns.compare: Compare CTAs, upload prompts, form complexity and trust placement.
patterns.when: For configurable manufacturing or commodity services.

patterns.title: A single service, one buyer path
patterns.question: How do service detail pages qualify the request and drive action?
patterns.principle: Keep technical capability and the next step in the same visual hierarchy.
patterns.compare: Compare proof close to CTAs and service-specific value proposition.
patterns.when: For CNC, 3D printing and design engineering.

patterns.title: Selling complex SaaS
patterns.question: How can software teams present a demo and self-serve option without fighting each other?
patterns.principle: Use actual product interfaces, differentiated action labels and role-based messaging.
patterns.compare: Compare dual CTAs, product demonstrations and onboarding cues.
patterns.when: For enterprise software products and business operations.

patterns.title: One company, many buyers
patterns.question: How do platforms serve industries and teams with different needs?
patterns.principle: Segment by audience or goal early, while preserving a common service identity.
patterns.compare: Compare first-screen paths, taxonomy and distinct conversion intents.
patterns.when: For multi-industry suppliers and platform businesses.

patterns.title: Let projects do the talking
patterns.question: When can real work replace generic credibility statements?
patterns.principle: Give documented outcomes strong visual weight and clear source context.
patterns.compare: Compare project photography, information summaries and depth of links.
patterns.when: For architecture, engineering and custom projects.

patterns.title: Case-study storytelling
patterns.question: How do case studies turn complex work into convincing proof?
patterns.principle: Link the client's challenge, applied approach and final outcome.
patterns.compare: Compare how projects are introduced before technical details.
patterns.when: For engineering services, product design and industrial consulting.

patterns.title: Operational proof at scale
patterns.question: Which proof points demonstrate actual capacity without empty claims?
patterns.principle: Tie quantified outcomes or network scale to the buyer's use case.
patterns.compare: Compare evidence hierarchy and placement within the page.
patterns.when: For logistics, manufacturing and infrastructure.

patterns.title: Engineering credibility
patterns.question: How do technically demanding buyers decide if a provider is real?
patterns.principle: Show traceable capabilities, detailed applications and product-domain expertise.
patterns.compare: Compare technical specificity rather than superficial badge counts.
patterns.when: For precision engineering, electronics and sensors.

patterns.title: Explain the delivery process
patterns.question: How can a long operational process become a clear, scannable sequence?
patterns.principle: Reveal steps, handoffs and output artifacts in a buyer-friendly order.
patterns.compare: Compare timelines, arrows, progressive disclosure and evidence.
patterns.when: For custom manufacturing and product development.

patterns.title: From design to delivery
patterns.question: How do you present multidisciplinary work as one coherent engagement?
patterns.principle: Connect design, engineering, production and delivery through a continuous narrative.
patterns.compare: Compare service connections and process articulation.
patterns.when: For integrated development, factory and supply-chain services.

patterns.title: The process is the story
patterns.question: When should the technical process itself become the visual narrative?
patterns.principle: Use real production stages and industrial context as proof.
patterns.compare: Compare production imagery, explanations and sequence framing.
patterns.when: For new materials, automation and manufacturing innovation.

patterns.title: Beyond the generic company intro
patterns.question: How can a B2B firm express a recognizable point of view?
patterns.principle: Use an explicit idea or methodology and support it with actual work.
patterns.compare: Compare narrative voice against concrete service information.
patterns.when: For consultancies, studios and technical companies.
